# /crav1-refresh-system-notes

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Keep the picture current](../../from-refresh-system-notes.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-refresh-system-notes/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Update the picture in docs/system/ when something was added: add what is new to the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect, and do not rewrite what is there.

When something was added, **[`/crav1-refresh-system-notes`](crav1-refresh-system-notes.md)** updates the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect. It adds what is new and does not rewrite what is already there. It does not design the change and does not build it. It can run on its own. Spark, ideas, intake, match, and the siblings that already append a glossary row also run this update. They do not rewrite existing glossary rows. Some commands ask at the end of the run whether to run it, and do not run it: [`/crav1-build-features`](crav1-build-features.md) when a slice is marked done or retired, [`/crav1-fix-bug`](crav1-fix-bug.md) and [`/crav1-fix-build-gaps`](crav1-fix-build-gaps.md) when the fix changes how the parts connect, [`/crav1-read-environment`](crav1-read-environment.md) after marks lines are added, and [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) once at the end of a read-environment or suggest-tests handoff. [`/crav1-build-tasks`](crav1-build-tasks.md) do not ask.

Adds what is new to the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect. Does not rewrite what is already there. Does not design the change or build it. Can run on its own. Spark, ideas, intake, match, match-dump, and add-to-spec run this same update and still do not rewrite existing glossary rows.

## Runs when

Something was added; catch the picture up. Called by the user and by [`/crav1-read-environment`](crav1-read-environment.md) for a confirmed system section.

## Reads

In short: The picture and what the spec states.

Reads the picture and what a spec already states.

## Writes

In short: New lines on the description, diagram, and connections, `Synced at` (repo cell or slice line), and a cleared, narrowed, or routed research mark when pointed at an updated note.

Writes new lines on the short description, the context diagram, and how the parts connect. When this run reads a whole repo, sets that repo's `Synced at` cell and touches only those repos. When this run reads only one slice, leaves that column alone and writes or updates `Synced at: <repo> <branch>@<short sha>, <date>` on that slice's `spec.md`. Reading specs does not set it. A consumer measuring drift uses the older of the repo column and the slice line, and an empty value means unknown, so fall back to spec file commit dates. When pointed at an updated note in `docs/research/`, checks each listed point and clears, narrows, or routes it. An older mark with no point lines is split into the hits it was made from. It also routes the note's own open questions when the answer lies outside the note's owner, including when the mark clears. It does not ask the user.

## Does not

Leaves existing picture lines, glossary rows, design, and build alone.

Limits and exceptions: spark, ideas, intake, match, match-dump, and add-to-spec run this picture update on the pass that appends a glossary row. Repos-to-spec updates the picture in its own pass. Complete-features, fix-bug, fix-build-gaps, read-environment, and the add-to-spec handoffs from read-environment and suggest-tests-for-code may ask and do not run this command. Implement-task and build-tasks do not ask. It does not commit a cleared research mark.
